Let
\[
\rho=\operatorname{root}_{(1/11,\,1/10)}P.
\]
I claim the unique compatible value is
\[
\boxed{\tau=\rho}.
\]

For even powers, write
\[
r_k=\int_{-1}^1 x^{2k}\,d\mu_\tau(x)
=\frac2{2k+1}+\frac{2\tau}{2k+3}+2\tau .
\]
The three-point Gaussian rule has nodes \(-a_\tau,0,a_\tau\). Exactness for \(1,x^2,x^4\) gives
\[
a_\tau^2=\frac{r_2}{r_1}
=\frac{21+120\tau}{35+126\tau}.
\]
Set
\[
u=a_\tau^2,\qquad v=b^2.
\]
The seven-node rule is exact through degree \(11\) iff, in the variable \(s=x^2\), the four-node rule at \(0,v,u,1\) is exact through degree \(5\). Hence the node polynomial
\[
N(s)=s(s-1)(s-u)(s-v)
\]
must satisfy
\[
\int N(s)\,d\nu(s)=0,\qquad \int sN(s)\,d\nu(s)=0,
\]
where \(\int s^k\,d\nu=r_k\).

The first condition is linear in \(v\), and gives
\[
v=
\frac{
\frac{56}{9}+\frac{108688}{495}\tau+\frac{26344}{33}\tau^2+\frac{3504}{11}\tau^3
}{
(35+126\tau)\left(\frac85+\frac{160}{9}\tau+\frac{40}{7}\tau^2\right)
}.
\]
Substituting this into the second condition gives, after cancellation of a strictly nonzero factor for \(\tau>0\),
\[
P(\tau)=0.
\]
Since
\[
P'(\tau)=1431900\tau^3+8005950\tau^2+7100300\tau+120890>0
\]
for \(\tau>0\), \(P\) has at most one positive root. Also
\[
P(1/11)<0,\qquad P(1/10)>0,
\]
so there is exactly one positive root, namely \(\rho=\operatorname{root}_{(1/11,1/10)}P\).

At this value,
\[
a_\rho=\sqrt{\frac{21+120\rho}{35+126\rho}},
\]
and
\[
b=\sqrt{
\frac{
\frac{56}{9}+\frac{108688}{495}\rho+\frac{26344}{33}\rho^2+\frac{3504}{11}\rho^3
}{
(35+126\rho)\left(\frac85+\frac{160}{9}\rho+\frac{40}{7}\rho^2\right)
}}.
\]
Numerically,
\[
\rho\approx0.0986253989850833,\quad
a_\rho\approx0.832064348788215,\quad
b\approx0.471539666133636,
\]
so \(0<b<a_\rho\).

If \(\alpha=2A,\beta=2B,\gamma=2C,\delta=D\), then
\[
\alpha+\beta v^k+\gamma u^k=r_k\qquad(k=1,2,3),
\]
and \(\delta=r_0-\alpha-\beta-\gamma\). Equivalently,
\[
\alpha=\frac{r_3-(u+v)r_2+uvr_1}{(1-u)(1-v)},
\]
\[
\beta=\frac{r_3-(1+u)r_2+ur_1}{v(v-1)(v-u)},
\]
\[
\gamma=\frac{r_3-(1+v)r_2+vr_1}{u(u-1)(u-v)},
\]
\[
\delta=r_0-\alpha-\beta-\gamma.
\]
At \(\tau=\rho\), these are positive:
\[
A\approx0.150208804680725,\quad
B\approx0.442243909413138,\quad
C\approx0.293417747226698,\quad
D\approx0.491260141319100.
\]

Uniqueness follows because any compatible rule forces \(P(\tau)=0\), \(P\) has only the one positive root \(\rho\), then \(v=b^2\) is forced by the first moment condition, and the weights are forced by the Vandermonde system above.

Thus the required final answer is
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{root}_{(1/11,\,1/10)}P}.
\]
